<!-- Generated by scripts/build-site-pages.py from docs/run-as-a-service.md — do not edit. Edit the source page and re-run the script; site_pages_mirror_is_current fails if this file is stale. -->

Use this page to keep sipnab running under systemd on a Linux server: a capture
that survives a reboot and an SSH disconnect, or a listener that other tools
reach over the network.

It covers:

- the unit the `.deb` and `.rpm` packages install, and how to change it;
- a unit of your own, for an install from the installer or a tarball;
- where the log goes, and what `--syslog` sends;
- what each signal does, and how a change to the configuration takes effect;
- where a crash report goes under a service;
- rotating the audit and provenance files;
- reading a service that does not start;
- checking that a running service is healthy.

Every output on this page comes from sipnab 0.5.232 from the arm64 `.deb`,
installed with `apt` on Debian 13 with systemd 257, unless a section
says otherwise.

## Before you start

- **A Linux host with systemd.** macOS and other platforms are not covered here.
- **sipnab installed.** See [Installing sipnab](@/docs/install.md). The `.deb` and
  `.rpm` packages install the unit and create the `sipnab` user. The installer
  and the tarballs install the binary only.
- **Nothing to change on the SIP server** for a capture of the host's own
  interfaces. A HEP listener needs the SIP server's HEP tracing pointed at it:
  see [Wire HEP from your SIP stack to a central
  sipnab](@/docs/cookbook.md#wire-hep-from-your-sip-stack-to-a-central-sipnab).
- **A firewall rule** for any port you bind to a routable address. A unit that
  binds only `127.0.0.1` needs none.

## Start the packaged unit

The `.deb` and `.rpm` packages install `sipnab.service` and leave it stopped.
It runs:

```text
/usr/bin/sipnab -N -d any --no-cli-print --syslog --metrics 127.0.0.1:9090
```

- `-N -d any` captures on every interface, headless.
- `--no-cli-print` keeps the per-message stream out of the journal.
- `--syslog` sends security alerts to syslog. See [Where the log goes](#where-the-log-goes).
- `--metrics 127.0.0.1:9090` serves Prometheus metrics on loopback.
- The unit runs as the `sipnab` user, with `CAP_NET_RAW` and `CAP_NET_ADMIN`
  as ambient capabilities. Nothing in it runs as root.
- It may write only to `/var/lib/sipnab` (`StateDirectory=sipnab`, mode 0700).

Enable it and start it:

```bash
sudo systemctl enable --now sipnab
```

### Check it worked

Ask systemd for its state:

```bash
systemctl status sipnab --no-pager
```

```text
● sipnab.service - sipnab SIP/RTP capture and analysis daemon
     Loaded: loaded (/usr/lib/systemd/system/sipnab.service; enabled; preset: enabled)
     Active: active (running) since Tue 2026-11-03 14:34:43 UTC; 3s ago
   Main PID: 218 (sipnab)
     CGroup: /system.slice/sipnab.service
             └─218 /usr/bin/sipnab -N -d any --no-cli-print --syslog --metrics 127.0.0.1:9090
```

Read its startup lines. The first line, the generated capture filter, is long
and left out here:

```bash
journalctl -u sipnab --no-pager -o cat
```

```text
INFO sipnab::capture::live: Capturing on 'any' (link_type=113, snaplen=65535)
INFO sipnab::security::alerting: Syslog output enabled (facility=LOCAL0)
INFO sipnab::output::prometheus_server: Prometheus metrics server listening on 127.0.0.1:9090
```

Scrape the metrics endpoint:

```bash
curl -s 127.0.0.1:9090/metrics | head -3
```

```text
# HELP sipnab_responses_total Total SIP responses by code class
# TYPE sipnab_responses_total counter
sipnab_responses_total{code="1xx"} 0
```

Confirm it runs as `sipnab` and holds only the two capabilities:

```bash
# Run all of these, in order.
ps -o user=,args= -C sipnab
grep CapEff "/proc/$(pgrep -x sipnab)/status"
```

```text
sipnab   /usr/bin/sipnab -N -d any --no-cli-print --syslog --metrics 127.0.0.1:9090
CapEff:	0000000000003000
```

`0x3000` is bit 12 (`CAP_NET_ADMIN`) and bit 13 (`CAP_NET_RAW`).

Prometheus also listens on port 9090 by default. On a host that runs both,
move one of them, for example with `--metrics 127.0.0.1:9100` in a drop-in.

## Change the packaged unit with a drop-in

A package upgrade replaces `/usr/lib/systemd/system/sipnab.service`. Put your
changes in a drop-in, which the upgrade leaves alone. A drop-in that changes the
command clears `ExecStart=` first, then gives the whole new command.

This drop-in turns on the REST API on every address. sipnab refuses a routable
`--api` with no credential, so the signing key comes from a file that only root
reads. systemd reads that file before it starts sipnab, so the key never
appears in the process list.

- Write the signing key:

  ```bash
  sudo sh -c 'umask 077; printf "SIPNAB_API_SIGNING_KEY=%s\n" "$(openssl rand -hex 32)" > /etc/sipnab/api.env'
  ```

- Create the drop-in. `sudo systemctl edit sipnab` writes the same lines to
  a drop-in named `override.conf`, through an editor:

  ```bash
  # Run all of these, in order.
  sudo mkdir -p /etc/systemd/system/sipnab.service.d
  sudo tee /etc/systemd/system/sipnab.service.d/api.conf >/dev/null <<'EOF'
  [Service]
  EnvironmentFile=/etc/sipnab/api.env
  ExecStart=
  ExecStart=/usr/bin/sipnab -N -d any --no-cli-print --syslog --metrics 127.0.0.1:9090 \
      --api 0.0.0.0:8080 --api-allowed-host capture01.example.net
  EOF
  ```

- Load it and restart:

  ```bash
  # Run all of these, in order.
  sudo systemctl daemon-reload
  sudo systemctl restart sipnab
  ```

Check it: mint a token from the same key, then ask for the statistics with
and without it.

```bash
# Run all of these, in order.
TOKEN="$(sudo sh -c 'set -a; . /etc/sipnab/api.env; sipnab --mint-token')"
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -H 'Host: capture01.example.net' http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/stats
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -H 'Host: capture01.example.net' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/stats
```

```text
401
200
```

[Bearer-token authentication](@/docs/auth.md#use-a-token) covers token lifetimes, scopes and
revocation. Serve the API over HTTPS before you hand a token to a client on
another host: see [Secure every listener](@/docs/auth.md#secure-every-listener).

## Write a unit of your own

The installer and the release tarballs install `/usr/local/bin/sipnab` and
nothing else. Give the service its own user and grant the capabilities in the
unit.

- Create the user:

  ```bash
  sudo useradd --system --home /nonexistent --shell /usr/sbin/nologin sipnab
  ```

- Write the unit. It is the packaged unit with the path changed:

  ```bash
  sudo tee /etc/systemd/system/sipnab.service >/dev/null <<'EOF'
  [Unit]
  Description=sipnab SIP/RTP capture and analysis daemon
  After=network-online.target
  Wants=network-online.target

  [Service]
  Type=simple
  ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/sipnab -N -d any --no-cli-print --syslog --metrics 127.0.0.1:9090
  User=sipnab
  Group=sipnab
  AmbientCapabilities=CAP_NET_RAW CAP_NET_ADMIN
  CapabilityBoundingSet=CAP_NET_RAW CAP_NET_ADMIN
  NoNewPrivileges=true
  ProtectSystem=strict
  ProtectHome=true
  PrivateTmp=true
  StateDirectory=sipnab
  StateDirectoryMode=0700
  LimitNOFILE=65535
  Restart=on-failure
  RestartSec=5

  [Install]
  WantedBy=multi-user.target
  EOF
  ```

- Start it:

  ```bash
  # Run all of these, in order.
  sudo systemctl daemon-reload
  sudo systemctl enable --now sipnab
  ```

Then run the checks in [Check it worked](#check-it-worked).

Two rules decide whether such a unit can capture and read its files:

- **Grant capture in the unit, with `AmbientCapabilities=`, not with
  `setcap`.** `NoNewPrivileges=true` stops a file capability taking effect when
  systemd starts the binary. A unit with `NoNewPrivileges=true`, `User=sipnab`
  and `setcap cap_net_raw+ep` on the binary fails to capture:

  ```text
  Permission denied on 'any'. This process runs with NoNewPrivs set (systemd NoNewPrivileges=yes, or a container started with no-new-privileges), so the kernel ignores file capabilities and set-user-ID: sipnab --setup-caps, setcap and sudo cannot take effect. Grant the capabilities to the process instead:
  sipnab.service: Main process exited, code=exited, status=1/FAILURE
  ```

  Add the `AmbientCapabilities=` and `CapabilityBoundingSet=` lines the
  message names. A unit whose `CapabilityBoundingSet=` leaves out
  `CAP_NET_RAW` gets `CAP_NET_RAW is not in this process's capability
  bounding set` instead. Add it to that line.
- **Every file the unit names must be readable by the unit's user.** sipnab
  reads token, key and certificate files as `sipnab`, not as root. A token file
  that root owns with mode 0600 stops the run with exit status 2:

  ```text
  --mcp-token-file '/etc/sipnab/mcp.token': Permission denied (os error 13)
  sipnab.service: Main process exited, code=exited, status=2/INVALIDARGUMENT
  ```

  Give the group read access and keep everyone else out:

  ```bash
  # Run all of these, in order.
  sudo chown root:sipnab /etc/sipnab/mcp.token
  sudo chmod 640 /etc/sipnab/mcp.token
  ```

  A file systemd reads itself, such as an `EnvironmentFile=`, can stay
  `root:root` mode 0600.

To confine the process further, sipnab has a Landlock file sandbox
(`--sandbox`) and a seccomp filter (`--seccomp`). Their reference rows are in
the [Security section of the CLI reference](@/docs/cli.md#security).

## Where the log goes

- **sipnab writes its log to stderr.** systemd puts stderr in the journal, so
  `journalctl -u sipnab` shows it.
- **`SIPNAB_LOG` sets the level.** It takes `error`, `warn`, `info`, `debug`,
  `trace`, or a filter such as `sipnab::capture=debug`. A headless run logs at
  `info` when the variable is unset, and at `warn` with `--quiet`.
- **`--syslog` sends security alerts, not the log.** Each alert goes to syslog
  with facility `local0`, priority `warning`, and the identifier `sipnab`:

  ```text
  facility=local0 identifier=sipnab priority=4 [ALERT] scanner src=127.0.0.1 method="REGISTER" ua="friendly-scanner" detection=ua_pattern
  ```

  The alert also appears in the log on stderr. Every detector is off by
  default and the packaged unit names none, so it sends no alert until a
  drop-in or `sipnab.toml` turns one on.
- **sipnab colors its log lines only when stderr is a terminal.** Under
  systemd stderr is the journal, not a terminal, so the journal stores plain
  text and `journalctl -o cat` shows no escape sequences. The same holds for
  `docker logs` and for a pipe such as `sipnab -N -I x.pcap 2>&1 | cat`. On
  a terminal, a non-empty `NO_COLOR` turns the color off. `--color` and
  `[display] color` set the SIP message lines on stdout, not the log.

  To check, look for an escape byte in the unit's recent log:

  ```bash
  journalctl -u sipnab -n 50 -o cat | grep -c $'\x1b'
  ```

  The count is `0`. A non-zero count means sipnab 0.5.244 or earlier. Set
  `Environment=NO_COLOR=1` in the unit to turn the color off there.

## Stop, rotate and reconfigure

sipnab handles four signals:

| Signal | What sipnab does |
|---|---|
| `SIGTERM` (`systemctl stop`) | Stops capturing, flushes the open `-O` file, prints the end-of-run summary, and exits 0. |
| `SIGINT` (Ctrl-C) | The same as `SIGTERM`. |
| `SIGHUP` | The same stop as `SIGTERM`, then exits 129. |
| `SIGUSR1` | Starts a new `-O` file at the next captured packet. |

A stop under systemd ends with lines such as these:

```text
INFO sipnab::capture::live: Live capture on 'any' finished: 0 packets, no drops
INFO sipnab::app::batch: sipnab: 0 packets captured, 0 SIP messages, 0 RTP packets across 0 streams
sipnab.service: Deactivated successfully.
```

**`SIGHUP` restarts the service.** sipnab stops as it does for `SIGTERM`, with
the flush and the summary, and exits 129 (128 + 1, the status a shell reports
for a process `SIGHUP` ended). systemd counts a non-zero exit as a failure, so
the packaged unit's `Restart=on-failure` starts sipnab again after
`RestartSec=5`:

```bash
# Run all of these, in order.
sudo kill -HUP "$(systemctl show -p MainPID --value sipnab)"
sleep 7
systemctl show -p ActiveState,NRestarts sipnab
journalctl -u sipnab -n 5 -o cat
```

```text
ActiveState=active
NRestarts=1
sipnab.service: Main process exited, code=exited, status=129/n/a
sipnab.service: Scheduled restart job, restart counter is at 1.
```

`SIGHUP` does not reload the configuration in place. A root start reads its
key files and looks up the `--user` account before it drops privileges, and
the process it drops to cannot read them again. The restart reads everything
afresh. 0.5.233 and earlier did not handle `SIGHUP`: it ended the process with
no summary and no flush, systemd recorded `Result=success`, and the service
stayed down.

The terminal interface stops on the same signals, leaves the alternate
screen, and exits with the same status. When its terminal goes away (you
close the window, the SSH session drops, or something kills the tmux server),
sipnab stops as it does for `SIGHUP` and exits 129, whether or not the
signal arrives. 0.5.234 did not: such a TUI kept running and using CPU
until `SIGKILL` ended it. The TUI of 0.5.234 also kept running after
`SIGTERM`, `SIGINT` and `SIGHUP`, and that of 0.5.233 and earlier after
`SIGTERM` and `SIGINT`.

A run that waits for input stops on the same signals, with the same status:
`--vcon-fetch -` while it waits for its uuid list on standard input, and the
archive password prompt. 0.5.234 and earlier: `--vcon-fetch -` waited for the
end of standard input and ignored all three signals, and a signal at the
archive password prompt exited 130. sipnab refuses a FIFO, a pipe or a device
given to `-I` (`-I /dev/stdin`, for example) at startup. In 0.5.234 and earlier,
such an input never worked, and the run could wait on it with all three
signals ignored.

The packaged unit has no `ExecReload=`, so `systemctl reload`
refuses:

```text
Failed to reload sipnab.service: Job type reload is not applicable for unit sipnab.service.
```

**A configuration change takes effect at the next start.** sipnab reads
`sipnab.toml` once, at startup, and reads its flags once. After you edit the
file or a drop-in, restart:

```bash
# Run all of these, in order.
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl restart sipnab
```

A restart starts a new capture: sipnab no longer holds the dialogs, streams
and findings of the previous one. Two files sipnab does re-read while it runs: a token revocation list
(`--api-revoked-file`, `--mcp-revoked-file`), when its modification time
changes, and a key log named by `--keylog` with `--keylog-watch`.

### Rotate a capture file on demand

`SIGUSR1` closes the current `-O` file and starts the next, numbered after the
first. In this run, sipnab wrote three packets, received `SIGUSR1`, wrote two,
received it again, and wrote one:

```bash
sudo kill -USR1 "$(pgrep -x sipnab)"
```

```text
INFO sipnab::capture::writer: Writing packets to '/root/cap/sip.pcap' (pcap, mode=raw)
INFO sipnab::capture::writer: Rotating output to '/root/cap/sip_00001.pcap' (seq=1, wrote 867 bytes in 2.035899678s)
INFO sipnab::capture::writer: Rotating output to '/root/cap/sip_00002.pcap' (seq=2, wrote 578 bytes in 2.027884822s)
```

- The new file opens when the next packet arrives, not when the signal does.
  On an idle link the file named in the last line appears later.
- sipnab buffers the open file. It can read as 0 bytes until sipnab flushes it at
  the next rotation or at the stop.
- To rotate by size or time instead, use `--split filesize:N` or
  `--split duration:N`, and `--split-keep N` to delete the oldest files. See
  [Run a capture that stops on its own](@/docs/cookbook.md#run-a-capture-that-stops-on-its-own).

## Keep crash reports

When sipnab panics it writes a crash report. Under the packaged unit the
report goes to `/var/lib/sipnab`, the unit's state directory, with no
configuration:

- The unit sets `StateDirectory=sipnab`. systemd creates `/var/lib/sipnab`,
  owned by the `sipnab` user, and exports its path as `$STATE_DIRECTORY`.
- With no `report_dir` set, sipnab writes reports to the first directory in
  `$STATE_DIRECTORY`. Outside a unit with a state directory it uses
  `$HOME/.local/state/sipnab`.

Prerequisites: a `.deb` or `.rpm` newer than 0.5.244, or a unit of your own
with `StateDirectory=`.

A panic under the unit then logs the file it wrote:

```text
crash report written to /var/lib/sipnab/sipnab-crash-20261103-143506-290-0.log
```

To keep reports somewhere else, set `report_dir` in `/etc/sipnab/sipnab.toml`
to a directory the `sipnab` user can write and the unit leaves writable, for
example a subdirectory of the state directory:

```toml
[crash]
report_dir = "/var/lib/sipnab/crash"
```

In 0.5.244 and earlier there was no such default. The service user's home is
`/nonexistent`, and `ProtectSystem=strict` makes the rest of the file system
read-only, so sipnab could not write the report:

```text
sipnab panicked at src/main.rs:297:9:
panic-selftest: intentional panic to verify crash handling
failed to write crash report: Read-only file system (os error 30)
sipnab.service: Main process exited, code=exited, status=101/n/a
```

The report's text still reached the journal. On those versions set
`report_dir = "/var/lib/sipnab"` in `[crash]` to keep the file.

To check this on your own unit, add `--panic-selftest` to a drop-in's
`ExecStart=` and set `Restart=no` in it, restart, read the journal, and then
remove the drop-in. `--help` does not list `--panic-selftest`: it panics as
soon as sipnab starts. [Send us a crash
report](@/docs/troubleshooting.md#send-us-a-crash-report) says what the report holds
and where to send it.

## Rotate the audit and provenance files

Three flags append one JSON line per event to a file and never truncate it:

- `--mcp-audit-file`: every MCP tool call;
- `--tui-audit-file`: every operator action in the terminal interface;
- `--run-provenance-file`: one line per run, at startup.

The two audit files stay open for the whole run. Rename one, and sipnab keeps
writing to the renamed file until it restarts. Rotate them with
`copytruncate`, which copies the file and then empties it in place:

```text
/var/log/sipnab/*.jsonl {
    weekly
    rotate 8
    compress
    delaycompress
    missingok
    notifempty
    copytruncate
}
```

Save that as `/etc/logrotate.d/sipnab`. `ProtectSystem=strict` leaves the unit
no writable directory outside `/var/lib/sipnab`, so add `LogsDirectory=sipnab`
to a drop-in. systemd then creates `/var/log/sipnab` for the `sipnab` user. An
audit file in a directory the unit cannot write stops the run with exit
status 2:

```text
--mcp-audit-file /var/log/sipnab2/mcp-audit.jsonl: Read-only file system (os error 30). sipnab refuses to serve MCP without the audit trail it was asked for
```

This run used the unit from [Write a unit of your own](#write-a-unit-of-your-own)
with a drop-in adding `LogsDirectory=sipnab` and
`--mcp-audit-file /var/log/sipnab/mcp-audit.jsonl`. After one tool call,
`logrotate -f /etc/logrotate.d/sipnab`, and a second tool call, the second
record landed in the emptied file as a complete line:

```text
-rw------- 1 sipnab sipnab 195 Nov  3 14:43 mcp-audit.jsonl
-rw------- 1 sipnab sipnab 195 Nov  3 14:43 mcp-audit.jsonl.1
{"args":"{}","caller":"127.0.0.1:38978 bearer-verified scope=full","elapsed_ms":0,"error":null,"id":"2","outcome":"ok","seq":2,"tool":"capture_status","ts":"2026-11-03T14:43:22.918525017+00:00"}
```

- `seq` continues across the rotation, so the new file starts at `seq` 2 here,
  not at 1. A gap is still a gap: compare the last `seq` of the old file with
  the first of the new.
- `copytruncate` loses a record that sipnab writes between the copy and the
  truncation. The window is the time `logrotate` takes to copy the file.
- sipnab writes the provenance file once per run, at startup, so any rotation
  method works for it.

## A service that does not start

`systemctl status sipnab` names the exit status, and the journal names the
reason:

```bash
# Run all of these, in order.
systemctl status sipnab --no-pager | sed -n 3p
journalctl -u sipnab -n 20 --no-pager -o cat
```

sipnab prints the reason it stops on stderr at every log level, so the journal
has it even with `SIPNAB_LOG=off`.

| Exit status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `1` | A runtime failure, or a value in the config file that sipnab refuses |
| `2` | A flag sipnab refuses, or a pair of flags it refuses together |
| `101` | sipnab panicked. See [Keep crash reports](#keep-crash-reports) |

[Exit codes](@/docs/cli.md#exit-codes) lists every code.
[Error messages](@/docs/errors.md) explains each message and what to do about it.

The refusals a service meets most often:

| The journal says | Exit | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `REST API refuses to start: --api 0.0.0.0:18080 is non-loopback but no --api-key / SIPNAB_API_KEY or --api-signing-key / SIPNAB_API_SIGNING_KEY was supplied.` | 2 | Bind `127.0.0.1`, or give a key as in [Change the packaged unit with a drop-in](#change-the-packaged-unit-with-a-drop-in) |
| `MCP HTTP refuses to start: --mcp-bind 0.0.0.0:18731 is non-loopback but no --mcp-token / --mcp-token-file / SIPNAB_MCP_TOKEN / --mcp-signing-key / --mcp-signing-key-file / SIPNAB_MCP_SIGNING_KEY was supplied. Bind 127.0.0.1, or supply one of them.` | 2 | Bind `127.0.0.1`, or give a token file |
| `metrics server refuses to start: --metrics 0.0.0.0:19090 is non-loopback but no --metrics-auth / --metrics-auth-file was supplied.` | 2 | Bind `127.0.0.1`, or give `--metrics-auth-file` |
| `HEP listener refuses to start: --hep-listen 0.0.0.0:19060 is non-loopback but neither a shared secret (--hep-auth / --hep-auth-file) nor a source allowlist (--hep-allow) was configured.` | 2 | Add `--hep-allow` with your SIP servers' addresses, or a secret |
| `--api-tls-cert (or [api] tls_cert) c.pem was given without --api-tls-key (or [api] tls_key)` | 2 | Give both halves of the pair |
| `k.pem: the API TLS private key is world-readable (mode 0644); chmod 600 it` | 2 | `chmod 600` the key, or `640` with the `sipnab` group |
| `failed to bind API to 127.0.0.1:18081: Address already in use (os error 98)` | 2 | Another process holds the port. `ss -ltnp` names it |
| `Permission denied on 'eth0'. This process runs with NoNewPrivs set` | 1 | Grant capture in the unit with `AmbientCapabilities=`, as in [Write a unit of your own](#write-a-unit-of-your-own) |
| `Permission denied on 'eth0'. CAP_NET_RAW is not in this process's capability bounding set` | 1 | Add `CAP_NET_RAW CAP_NET_ADMIN` to the unit's `CapabilityBoundingSet=` |
| `--mcp-token-file '/etc/sipnab/mcp.token': Permission denied (os error 13)` | 2 | Make the file readable by the unit's user |
| `--mcp-audit-file /var/log/sipnab2/mcp-audit.jsonl: Read-only file system (os error 30)` | 2 | Add `LogsDirectory=sipnab` and write under `/var/log/sipnab` |
| `invalid config value: [capture] snaplen must be > 0` | 1 | Correct the key the message names in `sipnab.toml` |

All four listeners' refusals of a routable bind exit 2, and sipnab prints
each before any capture opens. In 0.5.244 and earlier the HEP listener's
exited 1, after the words `Capture source failed to open:`.

**A misspelled key in `sipnab.toml` does not stop the run.** sipnab logs a
warning and ignores the key:

```text
WARN sipnab::config: Unknown config key: capture.snaplenn
```

Run `sipnab -D --config /etc/sipnab/sipnab.toml` after each edit. It prints the
same warning and the configuration sipnab would use, then exits.

## Check that a running service is healthy

| Listener | Route | Credential | Answer |
|---|---|---|---|
| REST API (`--api`) | `GET /health` | none | `200`, body `ok` |
| MCP over HTTP (`--mcp-transport http`) | `GET /health` | the bearer token | `200`, body `ok`; `401` without it |
| Metrics (`--metrics`) | `GET /metrics` | the Basic credential, on a routable bind | `200` and the metrics |

The standalone metrics server has no `/health` route: it answers `404` there.
Use `/metrics` as its check.

A capture that runs but sees nothing is not a failed service. See [A live
capture that sees nothing](@/docs/troubleshooting.md#a-live-capture-that-sees-nothing)
and [A HEP collector that receives
nothing](@/docs/troubleshooting.md#a-hep-collector-that-receives-nothing).
